2608.16852.title: What Do Compliance Detectors Read? An Audit of Activation Probes and Guard Models
2608.16852.paper_summary: Regulatory compliance monitoring in deployed language models is increasingly implemented as a legal and audit control, checking model outputs against written rules spanning data protection, healthcare, financial regulation, and platform policy. Such monitoring is meaningful only if a detector's verdict depends on the stated rule rather than on surface features of the scenario. We show this condition fails across the current class of compliance detectors, a failure we call rule blindness. Deleting, permuting, or substituting the governing rule leaves detection accuracy unchanged for every guard and activation probe we test, including a policy-conditioned guard that correctly cites the governing clause yet barely changes its verdict when that clause is swapped for its permissive counterpart. A purpose-built benchmark crossing two rules with two scenarios, so that neither alone predicts the label, confirms the failure under a design no prior benchmark rules out, and shows that step by step reasoning, not any fast detector we test, is what escapes it. Auditing at scale requires a retraining-free detector, so we introduce the Internal Compliance Score (ICS): a training-free activation readout calibrated from ten labelled pairs and scored by a single projection. We hold ICS to the same scrutiny as the guards it audits: a pre-registered criterion for beating trivial baselines is not met, and a bag-of-words model matches its pooled generalisation exactly. It remains useful because it is inexpensive, letting us audit four deployed guard models, an 8B zero-shot judge, and thirteen benchmarks, and it raises the mechanically verified pass rate when used to rank candidate responses, though an adaptive white-box attack removes this gain. We release the counterfactual protocol and crossed-rule benchmark so rule blindness can be tested in future probe and guard claims.
2608.16852.paper_summary_zh: 在已部署的語言模型中，監控法規遵循越來越多地作為法律和審計控制來實施，檢查模型輸出是否符合涵蓋數據保護、醫療保健、金融法規和平台政策的書面規則。只有當檢測器的判決依賴於所述規則，而不是場景的表面特徵時，這種監控才有意義。我們顯示這一條件在當前的合規檢測器中失效，這種失效我們稱之為規則盲目性。刪除、排列或替換主導規則對我們測試的每個守衛和激活探針的檢測準確性沒有影響，包括一個正確引用主導條款的政策條件守衛，但當該條款被其允許的對應條款替換時，幾乎不改變其判決。跨越兩條規則和兩個場景的專門基準，確保單獨的規則無法預測標籤，確認了在沒有先前基準排除的設計下的失效，並顯示逐步推理，而不是我們測試的任何快速檢測器，是逃避它的原因。大規模審計需要無需重新訓練的檢測器，因此我們引入了內部合規得分（ICS）：一個從十對標記樣本中校準的無需訓練的激活讀出，並通過單一投影進行評分。我們對ICS進行與其審計的守衛相同的審查：未滿足超越微不足道基準的預註冊標準，且一個詞袋模型恰好匹配其聚合的概括。它仍然有用，因為它成本低廉，使我們能夠審計四個已部署的守衛模型、一個8B零樣本法官和十三個基準，並且在用於排名候選響應時提高了機械驗證的通過率，儘管自適應白盒攻擊消除了這一增益。我們發布了反事實協議和交叉規則基準，以便未來能夠測試規則盲目性在探針和守衛聲明中的表現。
